title: Portfolio Transfers | Servicing Transfer & Loan Book Migration | Veteran Loan Servicing
description: Servicing transfers for commercial loan portfolios: transfer-in from a prior servicer, borrower notification, data validation, and disbursement continuity.
lede: Whether you are moving a book off a prior servicer or acquiring a loan portfolio, the transfer is the moment borrowers and lenders judge the servicer. We plan it so collection and disbursement continue without a gap.

howto.name: How a servicing transfer is run
howto.description: The steps Veteran Loan Servicing follows to transfer a commercial loan book in without a payment gap.

steps.name: Intake
steps.text: Take in loan data from the prior servicer or loan seller.

steps.name: Validation
steps.text: Validate balances and payment history against the source records.

steps.name: Notification
steps.text: Notify borrowers and lenders of the effective transfer date.

steps.name: Cutover
steps.text: On the defined transfer date, servicing moves onto our platform.

steps.name: Continuity
steps.text: ACH collection and lender disbursement continue on schedule after cutover.

sections.heading: Process
paragraphs: A transfer runs as a scheduled cutover: intake from the prior servicer or seller, validation of balances and payment history, borrower and lender notification, and a defined transfer date after which collection and disbursement run on our platform.
bullets: Intake from prior servicer or loan seller
Validation of balances and payment history
Borrower and lender notification of the transfer
Continuity of ACH collection and lender disbursement

sections.heading: Controls
paragraphs: We validate the transferred data before the cutover date and keep a documented transfer trail. Payment instructions are confirmed so that the first post-transfer cycle collects and disburses correctly.

sections.heading: Reporting
paragraphs: You receive a transfer confirmation showing loans transferred, balances validated, and the effective transfer date. Post-transfer, the book appears in standard portfolio and disbursement reporting.

sections.heading: Benefits
paragraphs: A planned transfer protects the borrower relationship and the lender's cash flow, and gives a loan purchaser a clean, documented handover rather than an inherited mess.

faqs.q: Can you transfer in a book we just purchased?
faqs.a: Yes. We handle transfer-in from a prior servicer or directly from a loan seller, validating data before the cutover date.

faqs.q: Will borrowers experience a payment gap during transfer?
faqs.a: The transfer is planned so ACH collection and lender disbursement continue on schedule; borrowers and lenders are notified of the effective transfer date.

faqs.q: How are borrower payments handled after transfer?
faqs.a: Borrower payments are collected via ACH and disbursed to lenders on a scheduled monthly cycle, structured around NACHA operating guidelines, with a full audit trail maintained for every transaction.
